subject: Logic
title: The St. Petersburg Paradox
description: A quick win: understand The St. Petersburg Paradox.

hook.text: A coin-flip game offers infinite expected winnings. So why won't anyone pay even $25 to play?

buildup.text: Flip a coin. Heads on flip N pays $2^N. The expected value is 1+1+1+... which is infinite.

discovery.text: Daniel Bernoulli proposed the answer in 1738: people value utility, not just raw money.

twist.text: Your 10th dollar matters less than your first. Diminishing marginal utility caps what the game is "worth."

climax.text: The paradox launched expected utility theory—a cornerstone of modern economics and decision science.

quiz.question: What concept resolved the St. Petersburg paradox?
